blockers.claim: authorizationRecord.consentRecordsScopeShape.byteCap defines a total, closed class-discriminated shape for the action-class value actually serialized in each doctor-v4 consent record.
blockers.evidence: doctorV4FieldMapping.destinations.actionClass explicitly maps authorization CA-1-HOST-HEAD to consentRecords[].actionClass=CA-1 and authorization CA-4-HOST to consentRecords[].actionClass=CA-4. The byteCap variants then use predicates 'CA-1 or CA-2', 'CA-4-HOST', and 'CA-3'. Those predicates cannot belong to one discriminator domain: under the serialized doctor-v4 domain, CA-1 matches but CA-4-HOST does not exist; under the authorization-record domain, CA-4-HOST matches but CA-1 does not exist. The surrounding scope shape has the same mixed convention at targetIdentity (CA-1 branch but CA-4-HOST nullWhen) and endpointSet (requiredWhen CA-4-HOST). scope itself has no actionClass member, so the only serialized parent discriminator is the mapped doctor-v4 value. A conforming consent record with actionClass CA-4 therefore has no literal byteCap branch selecting the required send/receive shape, defeating the class-total machine schema even though the branch's internal members are now well typed.
blockers.requiredRepair: Choose one class predicate domain and use it consistently across every consentRecordsScopeShape conditional. Prefer the actual parent consent-record values CA-1, CA-2, CA-3, and CA-4, changing the byteCap CA-4 selector, targetIdentity nullWhen, endpointSet requiredWhen, and any other scope predicate accordingly. Alternatively define an explicit, total discriminator translation and consistently use authorization values, including CA-1-HOST-HEAD. Extend FC-BOUND-SHAPE with concrete parent records proving actionClass CA-1 selects acceptFromTarget, CA-4 selects send+receive, CA-3 selects null, and no legal serialized class is unmatched. Redispatch frozen successor bytes.
